_comment: Copy to tools/site.json and fill in for your rig. Empty string = auto-discover (PATH / standard install dirs) then fail with instructions. Any key can also be overridden per-invocation with QUEST3_<KEY>, e.g. QUEST3_QUEST_IP=192.0.2.10.
_device_comment: Which headset family this rig measures: a profile name from tools/devices.py (the profiles that exist are listed there; 'quest3' is the only one run against hardware so far). Empty = quest3. A profile carries what the headset-side samplers ask the device for, which artifacts they write, where its metrics files live, and which streaming client counts as a session -- so supporting a second headset is a new profile in that file, not edits to cell.py.
_ovr_metrics_comment: Only an override: the headset's OVR Metrics CSV directory normally comes from the device profile in tools/devices.py (the Quest 3 path, /sdcard/Android/data/com.oculus.ovrmonitormetricsservice/files/CapturedMetrics). Set this if your device keeps that directory somewhere else.
_headset_log_comment: Logcat tags streamed from the headset during a session into headset_logcat.txt. Default covers the VR runtime (VrApi, QC2Comp) and the streaming clients (VirtualDesktop.Android, OVRMediaCodec, VR_Engine, ALVR). A tag that never emits costs nothing, so leave it as-is unless a build is chatty or Air Link logs under its own tag -- then add it here (space-separated, logcat filterspecs like 'tag' or 'tag:W' are fine).
_presentmon_comment: Optional PC game-fps capture (see tools/Sample-GameFPS.ps1). Leave presentmon_exe empty to skip it. Not vendored -- download the console-app .exe (e.g. PresentMon-2.5.1-x64.exe) from https://github.com/GameTechDev/PresentMon/releases/latest and point presentmon_exe at it. No install/admin needed.
_iperf3_comment: Optional link-capacity check (see tools/linkcheck.py): measures the raw PC<->headset link with iperf3 before a session, so a bad session can be attributed to the radio or to the encoder. Needs TWO builds, both user-supplied and not vendored: iperf3_exe = the ordinary Windows client (or just install it from winget/scoop and leave this empty -- PATH is searched); iperf3_android = the aarch64 Android build that gets pushed to the headset to act as the server. Leave either empty and the check is simply not offered.
